title: Board-pattern readiness test — most-repeated question types
chapter: CBSE Class 10 Mathematics · Chapter 10 Circles (NCERT reprint 2026-27)
tagline: Practice questions modelled on past CBSE papers; not predictions of this year's paper.
disclaimer: Original questions modelled on question types that have repeated in CBSE board papers 2023-2026 and the Sample Question Papers 2024-25 to 2026-27. They are practice for readiness, not predictions of what will appear in any exam.
instructions: 40 questions. MCQ and assertion-reason: choose one option. Numeric: type a whole number (angles in degrees). No calculator.

patterns.T2: Angles: two tangents and the centre

S1.name: Tangent, secant, number of tangents
S1.tip: Secant cuts at two points; a tangent touches at one. Inside: no tangent; on the circle: one; outside: two.

S2.name: Theorem 10.1: tangent ⊥ radius
S2.tip: Tangent ⊥ radius at the point of contact (Theorem 10.1): OP is the shortest distance from O to the tangent.

S3.name: Tangent length (Pythagoras)
S3.tip: Tangent length: PT² = OP² − r² (right angle at the point of contact).

S4.name: Theorem 10.2: equal tangents
S4.tip: Tangents from an external point are equal (RHS congruence) and OP bisects the angle between them.

S5.name: Angle between two tangents
S5.tip: Angle between the tangents + angle at the centre = 180° (quadrilateral PAOB with two 90° angles).

S6.name: Tangent–chord and tangent–radius angles
S6.tip: ∠PTQ = 2∠OPQ: the chord's angle at the centre is twice the tangent–chord angle.

S7.name: Circles inscribed in polygons
S7.tip: Each vertex sends two equal tangent pieces. Quadrilateral: AB + CD = AD + BC.

S8.name: Concentric circles and chords
S8.tip: A chord of the bigger circle touching the smaller one is bisected: half-chord = √(R² − r²).

S9.name: Proofs and case studies
S9.tip: Repeating proofs: tangents at the ends of a diameter are parallel; a parallelogram circumscribing a circle is a rhombus.

questions.question: How many tangents can be drawn to a circle through a point inside it?
questions.explanation: Every line through an inside point cuts the circle twice, so none is a tangent.

questions.question: A line that intersects a circle at two distinct points is called a:
questions.explanation: Two points → secant; one point → tangent.

questions.question: At most how many tangents of a circle can be parallel to one another?
questions.explanation: Only the tangents at the two ends of one diameter are parallel.

questions.question: The number of tangents to a circle through a point outside it is:
questions.explanation: Exactly two tangents pass through an external point.

questions.question: The angle between a tangent and the radius through the point of contact is:
questions.explanation: Theorem 10.1.

questions.explanation: Both true; only one line through P is perpendicular to OP, so R explains A (NCERT remark after Theorem 10.1).
questions.assertion: At any point on a circle there is one and only one tangent.
questions.reason: The tangent at a point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through that point.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: In the proof of Theorem 10.1, every point Q of the tangent other than P lies outside the circle. This shows that:
questions.explanation: OQ > OP for every Q ≠ P, so OP is the shortest segment, hence perpendicular.
options: OP is the shortest distance from O to the tangent

questions.explanation: Both are true theorems, but R does not explain A (a 2023 board type).
questions.assertion: A tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.
questions.reason: The lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: A point is 25 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 7 cm. Find the length of the tangent from the point in cm.
The tangent from a point P to a circle is 12 cm long and P is 13 cm from the centre. Find the radius in cm.
The length of the tangent to a circle of radius 8 cm from a point 17 cm from its centre is:
The tangent from P to a circle of radius 8 cm is 15 cm long. How far is P from the centre, in cm?
PT is a tangent at T to a circle with centre O. If OP = 10 cm and ∠OPT = 30°, the radius is:
questions.explanation: sin 30° = OT/OP → OT = 5 (a 2023 board type, new numbers).

questions.question: Two tangents from P to a circle of radius 6 cm are perpendicular to each other. OP equals:
questions.explanation: PAOB is a square of side 6, so OP is its diagonal 6√2 (a 2026 board type).

questions.question: PA and PB are tangents from P to a circle. If PA = 9 cm, then PB is:
questions.explanation: Theorem 10.2: tangents from an external point are equal.

questions.question: In the proof of Theorem 10.2, △OQP ≅ △ORP by the rule:
questions.explanation: Right angles at Q and R, hypotenuse OP common, OQ = OR.

questions.question: PA and PB are tangents from P with ∠APB = 70°. Then ∠APO is:
questions.explanation: OP bisects ∠APB.

questions.question: PA and PB are tangents from P with ∠APB = 60° and PA = 10 cm. Find the chord AB in cm.
questions.explanation: PA = PB and ∠P = 60° → △PAB is equilateral.

questions.question: TP and TQ are tangents to a circle with centre O. If ∠POQ = 120°, then ∠PTQ is:
Tangents PA and PB from P are inclined to each other at 50°. Find ∠POA in degrees.
questions.explanation: ∠AOB = 130°, bisected by OP → 65°.

questions.question: AB and AC are tangents to a circle from A. If ∠ABC = 50°, then ∠BAC is:
questions.explanation: AB = AC → ∠ACB = 50° → ∠BAC = 80° (a 2024 board type, new numbers).

questions.question: Two tangents from a point are inclined at 60°. The radius is 4√3 cm. Find the length of each tangent in cm.
questions.explanation: ∠APO = 30°, tan 30° = r/PA → PA = r√3 = 12 (a 2024 board type).

questions.question: RJ and RL are tangents to a circle with centre O. If ∠RJL = 50°, then ∠JOL is:
questions.explanation: ∠JRL = 80° → ∠JOL = 180° − 80° = 100° (a 2024 board type, new numbers).

questions.question: The tangent at P makes an angle of 40° with the chord PQ. The angle PQ subtends at the centre O is:
questions.explanation: ∠OPQ = 50° → ∠POQ = 180° − 100° = 80° (twice the tangent–chord angle).

questions.question: A chord subtends 100° at the centre. Find, in degrees, the angle between the chord and the tangent at one of its ends.
questions.explanation: Half the central angle.

questions.question: TP and TQ are tangents from T with ∠PTQ = 80°. Find ∠OPQ in degrees.
questions.explanation: ∠PTQ = 2∠OPQ (NCERT Example 2).

questions.question: AT is the tangent at A to a circle with centre O, and AB is a chord with ∠OBA = 25°. The angle between AT and AB is:
A quadrilateral ABCD circumscribes a circle. If AB = 6 cm, BC = 7 cm and CD = 5 cm, then AD is:
questions.explanation: AB + CD = AD + BC → AD = 11 − 7.

questions.question: A circle is inscribed in △ABC, touching AB at R, BC at P and CA at Q. If AR = 5 cm, BR = 4 cm and AC = 12 cm, find BC in cm.
questions.explanation: AQ = 5 → CQ = CP = 7; BP = 4 → BC = 11.

questions.question: A parallelogram that circumscribes a circle is always a:
questions.explanation: AB + CD = AD + BC with opposite sides equal → all sides equal.
options: rectangle that is not a square

questions.question: A circle is inscribed in a right triangle with legs 6 cm and 8 cm (hypotenuse 10 cm). Find its radius in cm.
questions.explanation: Tangent pieces at the right angle = r: (6 − r) + (8 − r) = 10 → r = 2.

questions.question: A circle touches all four sides of quadrilateral ABCD. If AB = 8 cm, BC = 12 cm and CD = 10 cm, find AD in cm.
questions.explanation: AD = AB + CD − BC.

questions.question: In two concentric circles, a chord of the larger circle that touches the smaller circle is:
questions.explanation: The radius to the contact point is ⊥ to the chord (NCERT Example 1).
options: bisected at the point of contact
longer than the diameter of the larger circle
equal to the diameter of the smaller circle

questions.question: Two concentric circles have radii 10 cm and 6 cm. Find the length of the chord of the larger circle that touches the smaller circle, in cm.
A chord of length 24 cm of the larger of two concentric circles touches the smaller circle of radius 5 cm. Find the radius of the larger circle in cm.
AB is a diameter of a circle of radius 13 cm and XAY is the tangent at A. A chord CD parallel to XY is 18 cm from A. Find CD in cm.
questions.explanation: CD is 18 − 13 = 5 cm from O → CD = 2√(169 − 25) = 24 (a 2025 board type).

questions.question: The tangents drawn at the ends of a diameter of a circle are:
questions.explanation: Both are ⊥ to the same diameter.

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: Opposite angles P and O add to 180°, which is exactly why AOBP is cyclic (a 2023 board type).
questions.assertion: If PA and PB are tangents from an external point P to a circle with centre O, then the quadrilateral AOBP is cyclic.
questions.reason: The angle between two tangents drawn from an external point is supplementary to the angle subtended at the centre by the segment joining the points of contact.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
